title: Cursor
summary: An editor-centered starting point for reviewing AI changes in an existing repository.

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: With Privacy Mode enabled, Cursor says it will not train on Customer Data and that most provider requests use zero-data-retention agreements. Its docs describe safety/abuse review exceptions and models that require administrator approval before provider retention is enabled. BYOK requests still pass through Cursor's backend, and Cursor says its provider ZDR agreements do not apply to user API keys. Optional Cloud Agents temporarily store encrypted repository copies while a run is active and delete them after completion. Privacy Mode is available on Free and Pro, is enabled by default for Enterprise teams, and can be enforced by team administrators. Cursor's Privacy Policy excludes personal data it processes for commercial customers as processor; those agreements govern instead. Turning Privacy Mode off may allow Customer Data to be used or stored for improvement and training. No account setting, team policy, API key, model approval, Cloud Agent use or agreement was inspected.

facts.label: MCP support
facts.value: Cursor documents local stdio plus local or remote SSE and Streamable HTTP MCP transports; its Agent can use configured and enabled MCP tools.

prices.name: Individual Pro
prices.billing: Displayed monthly price; confirm billing toggle at checkout
prices.overage: On-demand usage is billed after included usage is consumed.

sections.heading: Review an existing codebase
paragraphs: Choose a change that touches both implementation and tests. Check whether you can identify which repository context the agent used and whether the final diff is limited to the task. The relevant benefit is a reviewable change, not the amount of generated code.

sections.heading: Define the spending boundary
paragraphs: Before increasing the plan, inspect the current included usage and on-demand controls. Separate the cost of an individual workflow from team administration requirements. The recorded base price is not an unlimited-use claim.

pros.text: Supports local stdio and remote SSE or Streamable HTTP transports.
The MCP documentation lists support for tools, prompts, resources, roots, elicitation, and the MCP Apps extension.

cons.text: Setup differs by transport: local stdio runs a command, while remote servers use an endpoint and authentication configuration.
Cursor asks for approval before MCP tool calls by default; run modes can change handling for allowlisted tools.
Privacy Mode is available on individual Free and Pro plans; teams can enable or enforce it for members.
Privacy Mode does not make Cursor offline: AI requests send prompts and code context to model providers, and optional Cloud Agents temporarily store encrypted repository copies while running.

faqs.question: Which MCP transports does Cursor document?
faqs.answer: The documentation lists local stdio plus local or remote SSE and Streamable HTTP.

faqs.question: Are MCP tool calls approved automatically?
faqs.answer: Approval is requested by default. Auto-review mode can run allowlisted tools immediately and routes other tools through its classifier.

faqs.question: What does Cursor Privacy Mode cover, and what should an account verify?
faqs.answer: Cursor says Privacy Mode prevents training on Customer Data and that most model requests use provider zero-data-retention agreements, subject to safety and abuse review and non-ZDR model exceptions. Requests made with personal API keys still pass through Cursor's backend and rely on the provider's terms for retention. Optional Cloud Agents store encrypted repository copies while a run is active, then delete them after completion. Teams and Enterprise can enforce Privacy Mode; Cursor says individual plans follow its Privacy Policy rather than the commercial DPA. Verify the account setting, organization policy, model approvals, API-key route, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement; none was inspected here.

verdict: Shortlist Cursor when reading and revising diffs alongside the code is your main loop. Validate the usage allowance against your own workload.
bestFor: Developers iterating on an existing repository
notFor: Teams requiring a fully offline workflow without further verification
migration: Export your rules and record editor settings before trying another tool. Keep the repository and its tests as the portable source of truth.
gaps: Verify the account's Privacy Mode setting and team enforcement, any personal API keys, approved models with provider retention, Cloud Agent use and applicable individual or commercial agreement; no account settings or data flow were inspected.
